notes: The session's web search allowance was used up after the first six searches of this part (one for each legislative candidate). Everything else was found by reading known addresses directly with the kit's honest User-Agent: each government's own site, the two state parties' sites, local party units' sites, the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (read on a scratch copy of the database with the files step), and campaign addresses that official or party pages link to. No search engine was read in place of the search tool. Candidates with no findings below are the ones this left out of reach.

The Minnesota Judicial Branch site answered both a script and the fetch tool with 403, and the Governor's site showed a CAPTCHA; neither was worked around or asked again, so the two judges (Ann M. Offermann, Karl L. Schmidt) have no findings.

Therese N. Kiser: the website she filed with the Secretary of State has no address on the network (repeated address lookups on 2026-10-01 found no such host), so no website is recorded for her. The only web presence a party page lists for her is a social media page, which is never a source.

party_support (a key the loader does not read): three listings where a party unit publishes its backing of a candidate for a nonpartisan office under a heading that is not the word endorsement ("Recommended Candidates", "Local Candidates we support", "Letters of Support"). The Senate District 43 DFL says in so many words that a letter of support is not a DFL endorsement. They are kept apart from endorsed_by so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision.

robots.txt: every page a finding below rests on, and every page used to tie a campaign site to its race, was checked against its site's robots.txt for the kit's User-Agent, the way the kit's own reader does it, and all are allowed. Four government sites ask scripts to stay out: Cook County, Swift County, Wabasha County and the City of St. Michael. A few pages on each were read before that check was made, which was this part's mistake; nothing read there is kept (so Braidy Powers, whose only source was Cook County's own page, has no findings) and they were not asked again. Wikipedia's search interface was asked eight questions, found nothing, and is also outside what its robots.txt allows a script.
Left alone because they refused scripts: the City of Eagan's site (403) and the Scott County Republicans' endorsed candidates page (403). The Wright County Republicans' older address answered 402.

Judy Seeberger and Josh Heintzeman are sitting legislators with roster records. For Seeberger the Legislative Reference Library gives a birth date the roster lacks and one city office; for Heintzeman only the website and a review item are recorded. No party page naming Heintzeman's 2026 endorsement was found (the Republican Party of Minnesota's nominees page lists statewide and congressional candidates only; the Crow Wing County unit's site was not found).

verifier_notes: All 36 addresses in this file were re-opened on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each after its site's robots.txt allowed it; all answered. 53 findings checked: 52 kept, 1 removed.

Website notes were reworded to say only what the site itself (or a page whose address is in this file) shows. The statements that a site was the one filed with the Secretary of State, or was linked from a city's or school district's candidate list or another party page, were taken out of the wording because no address was given to re-open; each site still names the candidate and the office or place on its own.
Josh Heintzeman's review item: the Legislative Reference Library's line was confirmed word for word. What our own roster shows was not re-checked here.

party_support (three entries) is not a key in the rules. Each page was confirmed to say what is recorded, under the heading recorded ("Recommended Candidates", "Letters of Support", "Local Candidates we support"), and none uses the word endorsement for these candidates. They are not endorsements and must not be shown as such; whether they are shown at all is John's decision.

The City of Crystal's page carries Therese Kiser's entry ("Therese Kiser - Council Member Ward 1") inside the page's tab data rather than its visible text. That entry also holds family and contact details, none of which is recorded here.
